findings_qualitative.value: CO(1-0) forms a large, irregular molecular ring (outer radius 7.9'' x 4.4'') associated with the stellar disk that avoids the bulge region

evidence.quote: We can therefore safely conclude that the molecular gas is associated with the inner disk of J2345$-$0449, and avoids the bulge.

findings_qualitative.value: The velocity field is regular rotation; Kinemetry residuals are small

evidence.loc: 4.3 Fourier-analysis of the large-scale velocity field
evidence.quote: gas velocities in the ring as probed by the line centroids do not show significant deviations from rotational motion within the gravitational potential of J2345$-$0449

findings_qualitative.value: Broad CO lines coincide spatially with the region intercepted by the radio source; no escaping outflow detected

evidence.quote: We do not detect any outflow motion at velocities exceeding the circular velocity of the ring

claims.hypothesis: The radio jet is responsible for broadened CO line widths in the molecular ring
claims.experiment: Single-Gaussian line-width map compared with FIRST radio contours, a toy beam-smearing model and the THINGS dispersions of other massive spirals
claims.result: FWHM = 70-180 km/s where the radio source crosses the ring; beam smearing negligible for intrinsic FWHM >= 25 km/s
claims.finding: Jet-ISM interaction is the most likely cause of the broad lines

evidence.loc: 5.1 Radio jets as origin of the broad line emission
evidence.quote: This makes it very plausible that the radio emission from the AGN is also the main responsible for the broadening of the emission lines.

claims.hypothesis: Star-formation efficiency in the ring is lower than in normal spirals
claims.experiment: Compared average and extreme Sigma_gas and Sigma_SFR with Kennicutt-Schmidt, Silk-Elmegreen and extended Schmidt laws
claims.result: SFR surface densities are factors 50 to 75 below the Kennicutt-Schmidt relation and offset in the other two laws
claims.finding: J2345-0449 falls off all three star-formation laws, in the regime of gas-rich radio galaxies

evidence.quote: We conclude that J2345$-$0449 falls off all three star-formation laws

claims.hypothesis: Rapid rotation alone stabilises the gas against star formation
claims.experiment: Toomre critical densities for sigma = 10 km/s versus 30 and 75 km/s
claims.result: Gas is near critical for sigma=10 km/s but broadened lines raise the critical density well above observed densities
claims.finding: Rotation alone does not explain the low SFE; jet-driven broadening can

evidence.loc: 6.2 Rotational support in the ring with and without radio jet
evidence.quote: It therefore seems that the rapid ring rotation alone cannot explain why star-formation rates in J2345$-$0449 are so much lower than in other spiral galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: Alternative quenching or energy sources (AGN radiation, star formation, structure, environment) can be excluded
claims.experiment: Energy budgets from [OIII] limit and supernova rate versus jet power; literature on bulge, bar and environment
claims.result: Radiative power is at least a factor 10 below jet power; star formation is over three orders of magnitude lower
claims.finding: Radio jet is by far the dominant energy source

evidence.quote: We conclude, in agreement with (cite: walker15), that the radio source is by far the dominant source of kinetic energy in J2345$-$0449.

claims.hypothesis: Molecular outflows fast enough to escape exist
claims.experiment: Search for line wings beyond the circular velocity
claims.result: No such component down to a peak rms of 1.2 mJy; 3 sigma limit 0.69 Jy km/s (5% of flux)
claims.finding: No escaping outflow detected; gas likely stirred rather than ejected

evidence.quote: We did not identify any such component down to a peak rms = 1.2 mJy in our data cube.

why_this_data.value: The ALMA program was meant only to detect CO in the galaxy and offers arcsecond-resolution resolved molecular gas data

evidence.quote: which was only meant to yield a detection of CO line emission in this galaxy

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Multi-component, non-parametric and prior-based line fits to isolate outflow components were tried but not robust at the available S/N

evidence.quote: we have tried to perform a multi-component fit to the line profiles, and also adopted non-parametric methods.

limitations_admitted.value: Observations are shallow and low resolution; deeper data are needed to probe non-rotational components

evidence.quote: Probing non-rotational components would therefore require deeper observations with higher spatial and spectral resolution

limitations_admitted.value: GALEX resolution (5'') only allows average star-formation surface densities

evidence.quote: Currently available data can only provide us with average values, because GALEX has a relatively low spatial resolution of only 5$''$.

limitations_admitted.value: The extent of 2MASS resolution and S/N may affect the measured bulge-disk radii

evidence.quote: it might affect the detailed fit results, in particular the measured radii

referee_caveats_inferred: alpha_CO = 4.3 is assumed uniform though the perturbed gas may need a much lower value (the paper itself spans 0.34 to 4.3)
SFR is a single galaxy-wide GALEX FUV estimate; Sigma_SFR per aperture is not measured, so the KS offset compares ranges rather than matched local pixels
Alternatives (bar, environment, structure) are excluded from literature properties, not tested with the data here
Jet kinetic power and jet lifetime come from a cluster cavity relation and carry order-of-magnitude uncertainty
Sigma_crit values in the text for sigma=30 and 75 km/s are printed with wrong units

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA data described as new proprietary data; ancillary data public

evidence.quote: We complement these new proprietary data with several publicly available data sets of J2345$-$0449.

missing_for_reproduction: Imaging parameters beyond robust and cell size (image size, masks, threshold, niter, deconvolver)
Calibration details (pipeline or manual, calibrators other than J0006-0623)
Photometry apertures and exact velocity windows for integrated fluxes
No code released; no numerical tables of aperture measurements
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Single ALMA 12 m execution (~20 min on source, one Band 3 setup); a few GB raw plus ancillary imaging of ~100s MB
reproducibility.score_reason: Single ALMA project code and numeric results are given, but imaging and analysis settings are incomplete and many steps rely on multi-survey photometry and literature inputs.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The ALMA data are described as proprietary and the recipe lacks imaging masks, aperture definitions and fitting configurations, so the key numbers could only be approximated.

methods_papers.why: CO luminosity to gas mass relation

companion_papers.why: Discovery of giant radio lobes, optical spectroscopy, inclination and stellar decomposition
Chandra X-ray halo, jet kinetic power
IRAM 30-m CO measurement and star formation estimate
Jet-ISM relativistic hydrodynamic simulations used for comparison
